description: Somos un equipo de desarrollo de software, queremos innovar dentro de del desarrollo de herramientas útiles que puedan optimizar los procesos de monitoreo o seguimiento dentro y fuera de la NASA, paso a paso entender las problemáticas que actualmente se viven y obstruyen el avance, mediante un software útil, rápido y fácil de entender.
summary: V.I.T.A.L.I.S. is an intelligent health-monitoring software that runs continuously for astronauts on every mission, regardless of duration or destination. Designed for crew members with no medical training, it requires no clinical expertise to operate: an intuitive, touch-first interface built for microgravity turns raw data into clear, actionable decisions. The software ingests real NASA flight data and live telemetry, learns each astronaut's individual baseline, and applies a deterministic triage engine to detect physiological deviations before they escalate. Anomalies are mapped onto an interactive 3D anatomical model, guiding the user to the affected organs and triggering step-by-step protocols — from routine monitoring to emergency response. A bilingual engine, offline-first architecture, and NASA-inspired cognitive and stress modules complete the system, ensuring astronauts remain healthy, focused, and mission-ready at all times.
details:
Functionality and mode of operation. V.I.T.A.L.I.S. (Vital Information Telemetry and Life-support In Space) is an intelligent health-monitoring software designed for offline use. It is intended for astronauts without medical training and features an intuitive, user-friendly interface. It operates continuously, processing real physiological data—including data sourced from NASA—and real-time telemetry at a frequency of 1 Hz. The system establishes baseline parameters for each crew member and employs a deterministic triage engine to detect deviations before they escalate. Results are visualized on an interactive 3D anatomical model composed of 172 meshes, allowing crew members to precisely identify which organs are affected. Furthermore, the system provides clear, step-by-step guidance—ranging from routine check-ups to comprehensive emergency protocols—complemented by timed animations. Its bilingual interface (English/Spanish), optimized for touchscreens and designed for microgravity environments, ensures usability in any mission scenario.

Benefits. It enables the transformation of a vague sense that "something is wrong" into immediate, evidence-based action, even when no physician is on board. By functioning entirely offline, the crew does not depend on constant communication with Earth. Additionally, it safeguards behavioral health through tools—inspired by NASA protocols—for managing sleep, cognitive function, stress, and daily routines, ensuring the crew remains mission-ready at all times.

Intended impact. It provides autonomy in managing astronaut health during any mission, regardless of its duration or destination; it reduces risks, enhances situational awareness, and offers support to the crew when they are far from Earth.

Tools and technology: Python 3.13, PySide6 (Qt6), VTK/OpenGL for 3D anatomy, SQLite (in WAL mode) for local storage, FastAPI/Uvicorn for the local service layer, and the libraries sounddevice, faster-whisper, and edge-tts for voice and audio functions. Data is sourced from NASA’s Open Science Data repository (OSD-575) and NASA’s Human Research Program.

Creative approach: We have combined a deterministic and auditable triage engine with a 3D body map and a proactive assistant, making decision-making both reliable and intuitive. The entire system has been developed to operate completely independently of any external connection, facilitating synchronization among crew members.

Factors considered: Ergonomics in microgravity (tactile elements of 48–54 px, light/dark themes), signal quality degradation, communication delays, and loss of link (with a priority queue—A>B>C>D—for data transmission to Earth), traceability of every threshold back to its original source, and a clear ethical boundary: the system serves as a tool for decision support and the monitoring of health indicators.
